summary: Tested POST /api/webinar/register with a random unverified email (test1783113585@example.com). Registration succeeds and is saved to DB. Detailed Resend 403 error is logged correctly with full domain-verification message. BUG: response returns email_sent:true even though the Resend call actually fails with 403.
passed: Registration record is persisted in MongoDB (verified via /api/webinar/registrations)
Backend logs '📧 Resend API Response Status: 403' as required
Backend logs the full Resend validation_error message including 'verify a domain at resend.com/domains' and 'omba.mp@gmail.com'
GET /api/webinar/registrations returns 200 and lists the new registration

failed.issue: Response returns email_sent:true when the Resend API actually returned 403 and the email was NOT sent. Feature spec requires email_sent:false on failure.
failed.evidence: curl response: {"success":true,...,"email_sent":true,"registration_id":"d4019023-..."}  |  Backend log for same request: '📧 Resend API Response Status: 403' + '❌ HTTP Error sending email to test1783113585@example.com'. Root cause: utils/resend_email.py catches HTTPError and returns False (no raise), but routes/webinar.py uses try/except and only sets email_sent=False on exception — it never checks the boolean return value.

action_items: Fix routes/webinar.py to use the return value of send_email(): e.g. `email_sent = await send_email(...)` (remove the try/except around it, or additionally check the boolean). Currently send_email swallows the HTTPError and returns False, so email_sent is always True.

Optional: log the same '📧 Resend API Response Status' block for 2xx responses too (currently only visible in error path via HTTPError handler; the pre-raise print does log it, so this is already OK — no change needed).
